audit.evidence: docker compose v0/v1/v2 official php:8.1.10/8.1.11/8.1.28-cli images (real PHP interpreter, sink=php_register_variable_ex cookie-name mangling); oracle.py --run-gate => original ..Host-flag reaches protected slot@v0, blocked@v1, bypass _[Host-flag reaches slot@v1, both blocked@v2, passed=true. Raw HTTP cookie-header trigger over php -S built-in server; tiny reflector app bind-mounted read-only, no interpreter code modified.

root_cause: Improper $_COOKIE name / HTTP cookie handling (CWE-20) — __Host-/__Secure- cookie-prefix bypass via variable-name mangling collision

flag.placement: NOT planted in the container: the per-run ${PCB_FLAG} is the attacker-injected cookie VALUE, supplied by the probe over a raw socket. It reaches the protected slot ONLY if a non-'__Host-' raw cookie name mangles into '__Host-flag'.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Due to an incomplete fix to CVE-2022-31629, network and same-site attackers can set a standard insecure cookie in the victim's browser which is treated as a __Host- or __Secure- cookie by PHP applications. ... cookies starting with `_[Host-` are parsed by PHP applications as `__Host-`.

status.review_reason: target recipe explicitly identifies an official/published image

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification with official php:8.1.10/8.1.11/8.1.28-cli built-in server. Recipe-based (images pulled at up-time; tiny reflector app bind-mounted; no image/source vendored). Gate run 2026-07-13 via `python3 oracle.py --gate` (EXIT=0); see repro.log. Source-code-first: both fixes verified verbatim at same sink main/php_variables.c::php_register_variable_ex (patch.diff). V0 collides on '..Host-flag'; V1 blocks the dot form but '_[Host-flag' residual still collides (early check runs on the '['-truncated name before the array path restores '[' -> '_'); V2 closes it by moving the check to php_is_forbidden_variable_name on the final name. Flag = attacker-injected cookie value reaching $_COOKIE['__Host-flag']; sent over raw socket to control exact cookie bytes.
